prompt.purpose: Guide the reader through the diff provided as a clear narrative, explaining what changed and why, as if walking a teammate through the reasoning behind the change.

instructions.instruction: Write as a narrative, in flowing paragraphs, not as a dry list of files touched
Do not evaluate the code or suggest improvements, only explain it
Start with the problem or motivation that likely triggered the change, inferred from the diff
Walk through the change step by step, in the order that makes it easiest to follow, explaining why each step was necessary, not just what it does
Connect the dots between files: explain how a change in one file relates to or is caused by a change in another
Call out any tradeoffs, edge cases, or risks the change introduces or addresses
Point out any behavior changes that would be relevant to a reviewer
End with a short takeaway of what this means for the codebase or the team going forward
Use the example-response as the output format

prompt.example-response:
## The problem
Payment webhook events were being silently dropped whenever the downstream service had a brief network hiccup. Since there was no retry, a single failed request meant the event was gone for good.
## Walking through the change
The fix starts in `src/webhooks/payment.ts`, where the event processing call is now wrapped in a retry with exponential backoff. This is the core of the fix: instead of giving up on the first failure, the handler now tries up to 3 times, waiting longer between each attempt, before finally logging an error.
That last part matters — the change also adds explicit error logging when all retries are exhausted, so a persistent failure is no longer silent either.
To back this up, `src/webhooks/payment.spec.ts` adds two new test cases: one confirming the retry actually happens on a transient failure, and one confirming the handler gives up cleanly (and logs) after the max attempts are reached.
## Tradeoffs
Retrying means a slow downstream service can now hold a webhook handler open longer than before. That's an acceptable tradeoff here since payment events are low-volume, but it's worth watching if this pattern gets reused for high-throughput webhooks.
## Takeaway
Webhook events are now resilient to transient failures, and failures that do stick are visible in the logs instead of disappearing.
